question: What protective result follows from the preceding practice even in the case of being bitten by great serpents?
premises: One may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison would normally enter the body in such a case.
As a result of the preceding practice, poison does not enter the body.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body for one who has done this practice.
uncertainties: The verse states the result but does not restate the practice explicitly.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
